scope: Targeted comparative study of six reference games, not an exhaustive story corpus or a causal popularity study. Facts are paraphrased; applications are our design judgments.

excluded_as_evidence.reason: Retrieval returned site chrome without the article; not used for substantive claims.

sources.coverage: Opening fair, meeting Marle, small actions and later consequences
observations: The opening begins at home and gives a local social destination.
Meeting a companion and investigating an invention cause the next journey.
Small optional actions at the fair have later consequences.
sources.application: Start with a local promise; make repairing the instrument and meeting Nell separate, consequential actions.

sources.coverage: Main journey and late companion sidequests
observations: New regions and recruits arise from the preceding problem.
Late optional quests return to established characters and places.
sources.application: Retain the existing 24-chapter campaign; actually show its causal debriefs and connect early questions to later personal chapters.

sources.coverage: Opening mission, aftermath, early character roles and combat
observations: A capable, equipped protagonist can work when the mission and stakes are immediately clear.
The aftermath makes the mission matter to civilians.
Party members have distinct tactical roles.
sources.application: The defect is unexplained privilege, not competence itself. Our chosen opening instead earns equipment, makes Rook confront his regulator, and ties Iona’s healing role to her patients.

sources.coverage: Opening language, character variety, music and emotional range
observations: The team discusses military context in the opening wording.
Different characters and contrasting emotions are central to the interview’s account of the game.
The opera is treated as a dramatic scene, not background decoration.
sources.application: Give characters specific social roles and let the player’s music carry a plot function through the festival and memory reader.

sources.coverage: Premise, thematic unity and hostile groups choosing common purpose
observations: The alliance is explained through an oppressive shared condition.
The developers discuss how characters with different backgrounds come together.
sources.application: Rook must choose a costly alliance; Iona joins for her patients. Joining is an event and a commitment, not an initial array of IDs.

sources.coverage: Failure, permanent progress, evolving relationships and resolution
observations: Repeated attempts retain multiple forms of progress.
Characters acknowledge experience instead of pretending it never happened.
The interview values satisfying resolution and voluntary return.
sources.application: Keep objectives and learned patterns on defeat, record the retry in the journal, give the player closure, and let return visits acknowledge the journey.

sources.coverage: Build variation, character-driven story and repeated discovery
observations: New combinations and story events support repeated play.
sources.application: Keep Mako combinatorics but reveal the vocabulary gradually through the fiction.

sources.coverage: Encounter novelty, formation interaction and avoiding stale repetition
observations: Enemy combinations create distinct encounter situations.
The creator emphasizes encounter variety and moving on after mastery.
sources.application: Do not turn early progression into mandatory grinding. Teach the alarm caller and repairer through a small encounter, then move the story forward.
